In article <363E8B90.7540@tatooine.com>, obiwan  <obiwan@tatooine.com> wrote:
>
>From all I've read, Ross is correct that the
>amount of the IMF bailout (ie Indonesia's
>debt) equals the wealth of the ruling family,
>of order $30 billion.  This should not be
>over looked as a factor in the current
>problems.  It may just be that it took
>a few of decades of embezzlement for
>Suharto to put the country in such a
>mess that even his repressive military
>could not quell dissent over it.
>
>This is not to say that agricultural advances
>and hi tech. investment may have a lot to
>do w/ Indonesia's current predicament. But
>the currupt represive Marcos-like regime
>is also another factor.

I flash on the following from TK :


> Suppose you asked leftists to make a list of ALL the things that were wrong 
> with society, and then suppose you instituted EVERY social change that they
> demanded. It is safe to say that within a couple of years the majority of 
> leftists would find something new to complain about, some new social "evil"
> to correct because, once again, the leftist is motivated less by distress at 
> society's ills than by the need to satisfy his drive for power by imposing 
> his solutions on society.
>


 The point is, if the ruling party were to leave 
 office tomorrow, at least according to TK, leftists would 
 find something new to complain about.

 Emmett
